name: Vector Gridiron
tagline: An NFL model that projects per-game PPR output for 646 players in the 2026 season, and publishes the week-by-week walk-forward accuracy it actually earned on 2025.
dims: 32-d MTNN v2 gated fusion (d_emb=32, 13 feature families)

headline_stats.label: Walk-forward weekly Spearman across 17 scored weeks of 2025 (last-4 baseline: 0.6539)
PPR points MAE on 5,412 held-out 2025 player-weeks (last-4 baseline: 4.616)
Players projected for the 2026 season, 21 of them rookies
Trainable parameters over 85 features in 13 families

insights.title: It beats the baselines by a little, then Week 18 happens
insights.body: Over 17 scored weeks of 2025 the model's ordering hit 0.6899 Spearman against 0.6539 for a last-4-game average and 0.6611 for season-to-date — margins of 0.0360 and 0.0288. The gain is unevenly distributed: the largest improvement over last-4 is QB's 0.0631 (0.4314 vs 0.3683), the smallest RB's 0.0213 (0.7251 vs 0.7038). On raw points the same story holds — 4.296 MAE against 4.616 and 4.523. And the per-week series runs 0.690, 0.744, 0.727, 0.736 … before bottoming out at 0.652 in Week 17 and 0.561 in Week 18, the two worst of the 17; the peak was 0.744 in Week 3. Week 1 is not scored at all, because the feature builder requires at least one prior in-season game.
insights.source: eval_backtest.json → overall.spearman / baseline_last4 / baseline_std / per_week, positions.QB.spearman+baseline_last4, positions.RB.spearman+baseline_last4, caveats[1]; projections.json → model.report.baseline_last4_mae, baseline_seasontodate_mae

insights.title: Quarterback is where the model is weakest, and it says so
insights.body: QB walk-forward Spearman is 0.4314 with a week-to-week standard deviation of 0.1524 — more than three times the 0.0402 sd of the overall number, and the lowest of the four positions against RB's 0.7251. QB also carries the worst points error (6.371 MAE vs 3.486 for TE) and the widest 80% conformal band at ±10.29 points. That is why Josh Allen, the model's overall #1 at 20.34 projected PPR per game, still ships a floor of 10.05 and a ceiling of 30.63.
insights.source: eval_backtest.json → positions.QB.spearman / spearman_sd, positions.RB.spearman, overall.spearman_sd; projections.json → model.report.per_pos_mae, conformal_q_by_pos.QB, players[Josh Allen].proj/floor/ceil/rank_overall

insights.title: By its own promote gate, v2 did not clear the bar
insights.body: The training harness scores candidates on a Composite Quality Score and refuses to promote below baseline + 0.5. This checkpoint recorded cqs 63.19 against a baseline_cqs of 63.16 and a promote bar of 63.66, with would_promote_vs_baseline set to false. Its MAE of 4.296 is only 0.017 better than the v1 reference of 4.313, and the shipped weights are the selection split — trained on ≤2023, early-stopped on 2024 at epoch 11 — not a full-data refit.
insights.source: projections.json → model.report.composite.cqs / baseline_cqs / promote_rule / promote_check / would_promote_vs_baseline, v1_mae_reference, selection.split / best_epoch, deploy.note

insights.title: Draft position explains about 17% of who actually delivers
insights.body: Across 1,156 charted careers the correlation between draft-capital expectation and career PPR-per-game delivery is 0.4175 — roughly 17% of the variance. Desmond Howard, pick 4, carries the largest negative residual in the file at -64.3, landing at the 9.6th delivery percentile; the largest positive is undrafted Arian Foster at +53.1 (96.1st percentile), with Tyreek Hill at pick 165 close behind at 95.0 (+48.5). Only 75 careers are labelled T0 and 80 T1, against 1,001 left unlabelled. And the sample is survivorship-biased by construction — 1,514 players were dropped for having fewer than 4 charted seasons, so as the file's own caveat puts it, the worst busts leave before accumulating a career.
insights.source: trajectory_axis_gridiron.json → report.fit.corr_expectation_delivery, report.careers_scored, report.counts, report.dropped.too_few_seasons, report.min_seasons, report.T0_examples[0], report.T1_examples[0], report.T1_examples[2], caveat_survivorship

insights.title: The same-name defect was measured for football, not borrowed from basketball
insights.body: A Wikidata probe of 2,707 corpus names found 117 where two or more age-plausible American-football players share the name. Football makes that ordinary: the pedigree expectation normalises by pick 262 (expect_log = 1 - log1p(overall)/log1p(262)), and the draft table resolves 377 duplicate names across 12,927 rows by keeping the earlier pick. Roy Williams is both 2002 R1 P8 DAL DB and 2004 R1 P7 DET WR; Zach Miller is 2007 R2 P38 OAK TE and 2009 R6 P180 JAX TE — each pair two drafts apart, so a close draft year is weak evidence. The age band is computed rather than asserted: 21 to 40, the 0.5/99.5 percentiles of 9,250 ages taken from names Wikidata returns exactly one candidate for, with the percentiles fixed before the first run (the hoops probe asserted 17/45, watched a 44-year-old rookie pass, then tightened to 18/42 against the very cases it judges). vector-gridiron's train_matrix.npz gsis id is direct evidence where the band is inference, but it covers 2016-2025 against vectors.json's 1999-2025, so one gsis means one person since 2016 and only a name whose entire corpus span sits inside that window qualifies. It acquitted 14 flagged names, 6 of them ones the suffix sweep could not (anthony miller, chad williams, dj moore, jesse james, mike davis, tyler davis), and on 5 of those the DOB pass had confirmed two people and was wrong. 101 arithmetic-flagged names minus 33 suffix acquittals minus those 6 leaves the 62-name EXCLUSION_SET — Roy Williams and Zach Miller both in it, their corpus spans of 2004-2011 and 2007-2017 falling outside the gsis window.
insights.source: gridiron_name_collisions.json → names_probed, colliding_names, PLAUSIBILITY_BAND.band / percentiles / n_age_observations / derived_from / why_computed, SUFFIX_SWEEP.arithmetic_flagged / acquitted / gsis_acquitted_of_flagged / gsis_note / confirmed_two_or_more / EXCLUSION_SET, colliding['roy williams'].corpus_seasons, colliding['zach miller'].corpus_seasons; gridiron_pedigree.json → report.draft_rows_read / distinct_drafted_names / name_collisions_kept_earlier_pick / expectation_field; draft_picks.csv → the two 'Roy Williams' and two 'Zach Miller' rows

game.prompt: Which player does the model project higher for 2026?
game.axis_label: Projected PPR points per game, 2026 season
game.explainer: Each number is the MTNN's projected per-game PPR output for 2026 under neutral conditions, built off 2025 form — a forward prediction, not a historical average.

rounds.reveal: The model projects Robinson at 5.2 catches for 62.6 receiving yards a game after his move from NYG, just ahead of Jefferson's 5.1 for 61.0 — and it lists Jefferson as Robinson's third-closest comp at 0.986 similarity. WR5 vs WR8.

Dart's projected 20.3 rushing yards a game beats Jackson's 13.1, and the two are near-twins in embedding space — each is the other's closest comp at 0.986. The model ranks Dart QB9 in tier 1 and Jackson QB20 in tier 2.

These two list each other at 0.99 similarity and share the same top comp, Colston Loveland. Pitts edges it on 55.6 projected receiving yards a game to 52.6, and 4.8 catches to 4.6. Both sit behind Trey McBride at 16.52.

Lawrence is the model's QB2 behind only Josh Allen, projected for 248.1 passing yards and 1.65 touchdowns a game to Mahomes' 235.4 and 1.51. Pedigree features carry 0.214 of Lawrence's fused tower weight versus 0.167 of Mahomes'.
A 3.54-point gap between two 2024 first-rounders. Odunze projects 3.9 catches for 48.3 yards a game and lands WR25 in tier 1; Harrison gets 2.7 for 33.2, WR53 in tier 2 and 248th overall.
Henry out-rushes Achane 54.4 to 44.2 yards a game, but Achane's projected 3.0 catches for 26.7 receiving yards against Henry's 1.5 for 8.5 is worth more under PPR. Achane lands RB7, Henry RB9.
Chase carries the highest projected receiving yardage of any player in the file at 70.9 a game. Opportunity features account for 0.187 of his fused tower weight, roughly double Rice's 0.096.
Fields projects 26.5 rushing yards a game to Burrow's 5.2, which more than covers Burrow's passing edge of 239.7 to 200.7. The model has Fields QB7 in tier 1 and Burrow QB14 in tier 2.

McBride is the only tight end in the model's top 50 overall, at #16, projected for 5.2 catches and 59.3 yards a game — the next TE is Kyle Pitts at #56. Lamb sits at #60 overall and WR13, at 4.6 for 56.4.

caveat: "No timestamped archive of published projections exists — the site only ships the upcoming week — so this is a backtest of the projection METHOD: the frozen pre-2025 checkpoint scored on as-of features built strictly from prior weeks." (eval_backtest.json → caveats[0])
